summary: Hrishikesh Terdalkar works in computational linguistics and Indology. He studied at Chennai Mathematical Institute and earned his PhD at IIT Kanpur under Arnab Bhattacharya, later holding posts at IIT Kanpur, Claude Bernard University Lyon 1, BITS Pilani, and IIIT Hyderabad.

Hsiang-Kuang Chou was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under Swami Shivananda. By 1960, he held appointments including Professor of Chinese at the University of Allahabad, Chancellor at Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy, and Lecturer at University of Delhi.

Hsiao-Lan Hu specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Hu completed a PhD at Temple University and became an associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy, attested in 2017.

Hsing Yun (1927–2023) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. He studied under teachers including Zhikai and Yinshun, founded Fo Guang Shan and served as its abbot from circa 1967 to 1985, and founded the University of the West.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.

Hsu Yun (1840–1959) was a Buddhist figure who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953, serving as its honorary chairman, and taught numerous disciples, including Hsuan Hua.

Hsu-feng Lee specializes in Buddhist studies. Lee earned a master's degree at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon, attested in 2017.

Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist master who studied under Chang Zhi and Hsu Yun. He founded the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association and the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, serving as abbot of the latter from circa 1976 to 1995.
Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held academic posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo from circa 1977 to 2007.

Hu Shih (1891–1962) was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cornell and Columbia under John Dewey, later serving as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

Huabei Tan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Tan pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Medawachchiye Dhammajothi, attested in 2026.

Huai-Chin Nan (1918–2012) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. Educated at the Republic of China Military Academy and University of Nanking, he held professorships at Chinese Culture University, National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University.

Huaiyu Chen specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. Chen earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser, joining Arizona State University as assistant professor of Chinese religions around 2006.

Huaiyuan Yu specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Yu earned a Bachelor of Laws from Xiamen University, an MSc from University College London, and became a PhD candidate at Xiamen University in 2023.

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. After studying at UCLA, He held posts at Zhejiang University, Stanford, Sun Yat-sen University (2017–2026), and served as Associate Professor at the University of Macau in 2026.
Huawen Bai (1930–2021) was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University from circa 1951 to 1955 and later served there as a professor, attested in 1999.

Hubert Decleer (1940–2021) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Étienne Lamotte at KU Leuven in 1975. He served as academic director (1987) and senior faculty advisor (1999) at the SIT Graduate Institute.

Hubert Durt (1936–2018) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology, having studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held long-term posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, the Hobogirin Institute as director and editor-in-chief, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Wendy Doniger and served as an associate professor in Comparative Studies at Ohio State University from circa 1998 to 2020.

Hugh Canning (d. 1927) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed an M.A. at Trinity College, Hartford, by 1910 and served there as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology in 1914.
